criterion: The home gallery shows twenty project cards floating at different depths around a chrome spine over the electric blue, with the focused card enlarged, upright and carrying a label pill.
evaluation_rule: The home is the page at the Italian or English home address. Yes when a live scene fills the viewport over a saturated electric blue, when flat project cards sit at visibly different depths rather than in a flat grid, when a vertical chain of rounded reflective bead forms runs through the centre, when one card is larger and faces the viewer squarely while the others recede in perspective, and when that card carries a frosted pill with a project title, a discipline and a small north east arrow. No when the home is a static image or a plain list, when every card sits at one depth, when there is no central chrome form, or when no card is singled out with a label.

criterion: Choosing Spiral in the formation switch moves the gallery cards from rings into a single receding helix as a continuous rearrangement, and choosing Rings moves them back.
evaluation_rule: The formation switch is the frosted two part control reading Rings and Spiral on the home. Yes when Rings is selected on a first visit, when choosing Spiral makes the cards travel from their ring positions onto one helical path winding into depth, when the travel is visible as motion rather than a cut, when choosing Rings returns them the same way, and when the selected part of the control is visibly marked. No when the arrangement cuts instantly between two states, when Spiral looks the same as Rings, when the control changes appearance without the cards moving, or when neither part reads as selected.

criterion: The Works catalogue grid floats slightly rotated project covers over a faint darker blue perspective floor, with the view switch at the top centre and the filter pill at the bottom centre.
evaluation_rule: The Works catalogue is the page at the works address in its default Grid view. Yes when the covers are small tilted planes rather than a flat square grid, when a faint grid of darker blue lines recedes toward a vanishing point behind them, when a frosted control reading Grid and List sits at the top centre, and when a frosted pill carrying the facet count sits at the bottom centre. No when the covers form a plain flat grid, when there is no receding floor, or when either control sits elsewhere or is missing.

criterion: Choosing a discipline in the catalogue filter narrows the covers in place with a rising staggered reveal, and every facet keeps its count in brackets.
evaluation_rule: The catalogue filter is the frosted pill at the bottom of the Works page that opens the facet list. Yes when the list offers All, Branding, Editorial, Type Design, Web Design and Packaging, each followed by a count in brackets, when choosing one narrows the covers on the same page to the matching projects, when the remaining covers rise into place one after another rather than all at once, and when a close control reading a multiplication sign closes the list. No when choosing a facet navigates to another page, when the covers do not narrow, when the counts are missing, or when the narrowed covers appear with no motion at all.

criterion: The enquiry form on the contact page names each invalid field beside that field before anything is sent, and every typed value stays in place after a refusal.
evaluation_rule: The enquiry form is the name, email and message form on the contact page. Yes when submitting a one letter name, a malformed email or a message of a few characters shows a message beside each offending field, when nothing is sent while a field is invalid, when a refused attempt leaves the name, the email and the message exactly as typed, and when each field has a visible label rather than a placeholder alone. No when the form submits invalid input, when errors appear only in one summary far from the fields, when a refusal clears what was typed, or when a field has no label.

criterion: The inbox table lists stored enquiries newest first with a status control on each, confirms a status change with a toast, and still shows the new status after a reload.
evaluation_rule: The inbox is the table of stored enquiries a studio member reaches after signing in. Yes when the rows carry a reference, a received time, a name, an email and a status, when the newest enquiry is first, when changing a row's status to replied shows a short confirmation toast, and when reloading the page shows that row still reading replied. No when the inbox is a set of cards rather than a table, when the order is not newest first, when a status change shows no confirmation, or when a reload restores the previous status.

criterion: A project page offers the previous project, the next project and a way back to the catalogue, and opening a project slides a full panel across rather than cutting.
evaluation_rule: A project page is the page reached by choosing a project card. Yes when the page shows a large cover, the title, the disciplines, the year and the client, when it offers a previous and a next project and a link back to the Works catalogue, when choosing next from the last project reaches the first, and when moving into a project slides a full width panel across the viewport. No when the page is a dead end with no onward navigation, when the transition is an instant cut, or when the metadata is missing.

criterion: The not-found page presents a broken television with a curved tube, darkened corners, clearing static and torn text, and offers a clear action back to the home.
evaluation_rule: The not-found page is what an address that is not a route shows, for example the address test. Yes when the blue screen is framed as a rounded tube with corners falling to black, when the surface appears bowed like curved glass, when a layer of static clears and the 404 text tears into horizontal streaks before settling, when the page reads 404 with a page not found line, and when an action returns to the home. No when the page is a plain text message, when there is no action back to the home, or when the television treatment is a still image with no live static.

criterion: The studio page sets the STUDIO word, the three eyebrow lines and the statement at display scale in one sans family, and lists six services as a two column list separated by hairlines beside a turning chrome sculpture.
evaluation_rule: The studio page is the long editorial page at the studio address. Yes when the word STUDIO is set very large, when three small eyebrow lines read based in Catania, since 2017 and the four disciplines, when the statement about defining attitudes is set at display scale, when the services run as rows with a label at the left and a paragraph at the right divided by thin lines, and when a large reflective sculpture turns down the centre as the page scrolls. No when the page mixes several typefaces, when the services are a bulleted list, or when there is no sculpture.

criterion: Electric ultramarine blue with white type carries the gallery, the catalogue, the project pages and the studio page, pure black appears on the letterbox of the not-found page, and grey appears inside the consent banner alone.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the ground of the home, Works, a project page and the studio page is one saturated electric blue, when type and marks on it are white, when frosted controls read as translucent glass over the blue, when the letterbox around the not-found tube is pure black, and when the consent banner is the only surface painted in greys. No when a second accent colour appears on the main pages, when the ground is a muted or navy blue, or when grey panels appear outside the consent banner.

criterion: Headings and paragraphs rise into place word by word and glyph by glyph, catalogue rows rise in a staggered wave, and the boot loader counts up from zero and wipes away before the scene appears.
evaluation_rule: Yes when the first load shows a full screen counter starting at a bracketed zero and counting up before white patches wipe it away, when headings on the studio page arrive as words or letters sliding up from just below their resting place, when rows of catalogue items lift in one after another, and when large elements settle with a soft ease rather than a linear slide. No when text appears all at once, when the loader is a spinner, or when every element animates at the same instant.

criterion: Keyboard alone reaches and operates the language switch, the Works view switch, the facets, the filter close control and the enquiry form fields, each with a visible focus state.
evaluation_rule: Yes when repeated Tab presses move through the header links, the IT and EN switch, the Grid and List control, the filter pill, each facet, the close control and the contact form fields in a sensible order, when each focused control shows a clearly visible outline or ring, and when Enter or Space operates each one. No when any of those controls cannot be reached, when focus is invisible on any of them, or when focus jumps in an order unrelated to the layout.

criterion: At a phone width the header links collapse behind a frosted MENU button that opens a full overlay reading CLOSE, the formation switch on the home gallery moves to the bottom left, and every route stays within the viewport width.
evaluation_rule: Check at a width of about 390px. Yes when the header shows a frosted pill reading MENU instead of the links, when opening it covers the screen with the links and the button reads a close label, when the Rings and Spiral control sits at the bottom left of the home, and when the home, Works, the studio page and the contact page scroll only vertically. No when the desktop links remain crowded in the header, when the formation switch stays at the top centre, or when any of those pages can be dragged sideways.
